findings.claim: The public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

In the group member row itemView, {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the member (Discourse.User) rather than the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the remove link is shown for automatic groups.

The item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate itemView template, so rows render without member data and remove can fail when the controller calls member.get(...).
A function has code paths that end without an explicit return and return undefined.
The group[usernames] parameter is now ignored by the API.
The admin group create and update actions read top-level params instead of group[...], with no compatibility path: legacy create gets a blank name (422) and legacy update silently sets visible=false.
GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array, which is not backwards compatible.
The PATCH /admin/groups/:id endpoint with changes[add|delete] is removed without documentation.
The '== 0' comparisons at lines 7 and 12 violate the .jshintrc eqeqeq rule.
totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which gives one extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 gives 3), so navigation can reach an empty page.
The next action clamps the offset to user_count instead of the last valid offset, so it can navigate to an empty page (e.g. total equal to limit gives offset == total).
remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which bypasses callbacks so the groups.user_count counter_cache is not decremented, unlike add_members which uses group.add.
remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, so the removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared and the group can still show as post flair.
add_members calls usernames.split(','), assuming a string; usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b yields an Array and raises NoMethodError (500).
The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' controller spec sends xhr :put to remove_member, but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing.
The limit and offset params on the members endpoint are not validated or clamped: negative values reach SQL and cause errors, and limit has no upper cap.
findMembers() is called asynchronously without its promise being returned or awaited from setupController, so the template may render before member data is available.
removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handler, so 422/500 responses give the admin no feedback.
The usernames input is not cleared after an add operation.

add_members calls group.add(user) without checking for existing membership, so adding an existing member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id,user_id) and raises RecordNotUnique (500), and earlier users stay committed because there is no transaction.
Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset.
The pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec still parses the old array shape, and no spec covers the new {members, meta} response contract.

group.save with render_json_error after add/remove is effectively a no-op, because membership writes already hit the DB via has_many :through, so the error branch only fires on unrelated group validation failures.
addMembers ends with '})' without a semicolon, which triggers jshint W033 under .jshintrc.
There is a stray semicolon after a block (if (!this.get('id')) { return };), which triggers jshint W032.
The routes provide the group id in params[:id], but the controller reads params[:group_id], causing a param-missing failure.
The Group#usernames= setter, destroy_deletions and after_save :destroy_deletions are now dead code in production; only specs call the setter.
The create action never reads params[:alias_level], although the form sends it, so the value is dropped on create.
add_members does not normalize usernames before lookup, so whitespace or blank entries cause valid users to be skipped.
The group/members.hbs template contains a stray closing tag with no matching opening tag.
The SCSS hardcodes the colors #333 and #aaa instead of using SCSS variables.
The guard in group/members.hbs checks model, but the loop iterates over members, so the table header can render with no rows.
findMembers builds its URL from the bound, possibly unsaved group name, so after the name is edited, paging/add/remove request /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json and get a 404.
The commit body is empty, contrary to CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement to describe breaking changes.
The offset is clamped in the next/previous actions and again in findMembers.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
